priorFindingsVerification.evidence: Read resolve-identity.mjs fresh line-by-line. Confirmed: passing a non-null, fully-constructed env object (per the spec's now-corrected worked examples, e.g. env: {HOME: '/Users/anicca', ANICCA_HOME: '/Users/anicca/.anicca'}) makes `const e = env || process.env` bind to the explicit object unconditionally -- the function genuinely never touches ambient process.env when this shape is used, which is exactly the property FIND-603 demanded. Walked the legacy-fallback branch: with citizen.homeDir='/Users/anicca/.anicca' and env.HOME='/Users/anicca', `effectiveHome === path.join(legacyHome, '.anicca')` evaluates true, correctly falling through to read the real, confirmed-present /Users/anicca/.automaton/wallet.json (I verified this file's existence and rotatedAt/privateKey fields directly). PROP-403e's stripped/launchd-style process.env Tier-2 test is a correct, meaningful test of the FUNCTION's own behavior. HOWEVER: the spec's own prescription for HOW the audit script is to construct env.HOME's value -- 'the coordinator host's own real $HOME, sourced from a registry/coordinator constant' -- names no actual constant, module, or schema field anywhere in either spec document (confirmed via grep: this exact phrase appears in exactly two places, both unresolved placeholders). This means FIND-603's underlying concern (an unmodeled, silently-load-bearing input to the resolvers) has been relocated from 'the resolver's own ambient process.env' to 'the audit script's own unspecified source for what value to put in the explicit env object' -- filed as new, critical FIND-701, since a Phase-2 implementer could satisfy PROP-403e's literal test while still reintroducing an ambient-environment dependency one layer up (e.g. sourcing the value from os.homedir()/process.env.HOME at audit-script startup).
